risks.description: An external project-generation run could leak credentials, exceed cost limits, silently switch models, confuse Provider connectivity with package installation, or fall back to Codex generation.
risks.response: Require environment-only credentials and explicit models, reserve every call in a process-safe budget ledger before transport, keep dependency authorization separate, record all terminal outcomes, and enforce zero Codex generation and repair calls.

risks.description: A benchmark could overstate project quality by leaking hidden acceptance, accepting file presence or self-tests as success, hiding first-pass failures behind repair, or exercising a support lane instead of the reviewed production route.
risks.response: Freeze ten identity-bound cases, use the Codex conversation production facade, keep evaluator inputs outside generation, require independent clean-start/runtime/persistence/integration/goal-fidelity observations, cap repair at two rounds, and report first-pass separately from final results.
risks.observed_outcome: PGBV1_BASELINE_20261014_04 completed with 0/10 PROJECT_PASS, 0 false-pass, and root failures CODE_GENERATION=4, RUNTIME=5, DEPENDENCY=1. The gate worked, but generated-project quality remains NEEDS_REWORK.

risks.description: An interrupted or resource-incomplete run could be mislabeled as a 24-hour reliability PASS, or blind acceptance could leak into model generation and inflate quality results.
risks.response: Bind each run to frozen identities, require one uninterrupted 86400-second interval with complete denominators and raw time series, physically separate hidden acceptance, scan all generation inputs for leakage, and retain failed/incomplete runs under distinct ids.

risks.description: Whole-run recursive telemetry can phase-lock with fixed arrivals and add O(total retained files) CPU and I/O contention, while unrelated host contention can make short scale medians non-monotonic.
risks.response: Use incremental per-project accounting with final exact reconciliation, retain legacy mode for A/B only, capture host CPU/memory/disk counters, and require a fresh >=4h first/last-two-hour validation before any new 24-hour run.

risks.description: A synthetic exception, endpoint-only resource snapshot, or partial completion could be mistaken for real recovery and sustained-load evidence.
risks.response: Require OS-observed worker termination, identity-bound recovery checks, fixed-rate arrival timestamps, complete denominators, sampled CPU/RSS/disk/handles/queue depth, and fail-closed run validation before any PASS claim.

risks.description: A candidate pytest process can inherit or resolve a deleted temporary root and fail only under a particular repository-test order.
risks.response: Run candidates in isolated mode with bounded environment, candidate-only import roots, and an execution-owned TEMP, TMP, and pytest basetemp; retain seeded shuffled full regression.

risks.description: A benchmark adapter, dead request worker, oversized context, or incomplete load denominator can create false confidence in end-to-end completion.
risks.response: Isolate benchmark consumers, classify durable external waits separately, bind async result admission to identity, retain exact outbound budgeting, and record every planned load outcome.

risks.description: Large legal dependency graphs or ownership sets can exhaust recursion depth or consume quadratic validation time before Provider work starts.
risks.response: Use iterative dependency traversal, sorted ownership indexing, scale regressions, and exact-request context budgeting at the shared Provider boundary.

risks.description: Requirements planning may spend five long attempts on the same pre-header failure without distinguishing Provider availability from payload sensitivity.
risks.response: Run ordered same-route probes, record privacy-safe request metrics, and stop after two consecutive same-class pre-header failures.

risks.description: Repository-wide Git inspection can block production before requirements or external discovery begins.
risks.response: Use canonical pathspecs, bounded read-only Git calls, a total capture budget, tree pruning, and fail-closed production classification.

risks.description: A selected executor may be present in support metadata while generated dependencies or runtime behavior silently ignore it.
risks.response: Freeze an exact integration contract before generation and independently validate dependency, AST API use, source identity, and runtime evidence.

risks.description: Incomplete or stale maintenance/security metadata could permit a vulnerable or abandoned exact version to enter an automatic trial.
risks.response: Require bounded GitHub maintenance enrichment, exact-version OSV evaluation, conservative conflict handling, freshness TTLs, and trust PASS before trial.

risks.description: Untrusted external metadata or package code could be mistaken for trustworthy execution capability or leak credentials during a trial.
risks.response: Allowlist endpoints, bound metadata and candidates, require deterministic filters plus isolated timeout-limited trials with a minimal secret-free environment, and fall back to Agent Build.

risks.description: CGKN may resolve a different DashScope account or API method than Attune despite sharing a model name and endpoint host.
risks.response: Prefer the shared QWEN environment contract, match Chat Completions payload semantics, and verify once through the canonical probe.

risks.description: A pre-build Provider stage silently replaces the reviewed route model with an endpoint-incompatible default, preventing the real result and provenance chain from materializing.
risks.response: Thread the resolved routing policy through requirements planning, test exact model selection and all provenance bindings, then perform one bounded live validation.

risks.description: Moving formal specs breaks a loader, test, or documentation reference.
risks.response: Use a specs-first compatibility loader, reference graph, legacy-path scan, schema validation, and compilation of all important flows.

risks.description: Runtime cleanup deletes local user data.
risks.response: Use git rm --cached only; keep local artifacts, workspaces, memories, and historical iteration files ignored and recoverable.

risks.description: Curated evidence is mistaken for delivery authority.
risks.response: Every promoted bundle carries a canonical status, limitations, reproduction command, and explicit support-only authority note.
